evals.prompt: Our clinic needs a staff inbox for appointment requests. Staff should see patient name, requested slot, and urgency; let them accept or decline. Include loading and empty states.
evals.expected_output: A backend-facing requirements note with context, data, actions, UI states, uncertainties, and open questions.
assertions: Names appointment requests and patient/requested-slot/urgency display needs.
Lists accept and decline actions plus loading and empty states.
Includes uncertainties/questions without specifying endpoint, HTTP method, or field names.

evals.prompt: For a support inbox show customer identity, latest message, unread state, and assignment. Agents can reply, assign, and resolve; handle loading, empty, permission denied, and partial customer data.
evals.expected_output: A structured requirements note for the support inbox, leaving API implementation to backend.
assertions: Covers identity, latest message, unread state, and assignment display.
Lists reply, assign, and resolve actions and all four requested states.
Includes at least one backend question and no prescribed endpoint or field name.

evals.prompt: The billing screen needs to show overdue invoices and let an account owner retry payment. What should I send backend?
evals.expected_output: A requirements document reframes the request as user-facing data/actions and invites backend input rather than dictating API design.
assertions: States overdue invoices and account-owner retry payment as UI needs.
Includes a relevant error or loading state.
Asks an open backend question and specifies no REST route or JSON field.
